info.name: Workdesk24 API - Modular Organization
info.description: Complete API collection organized by modules: Health, Auth, Public, App (Profile + Sync), and Admin (Users + Inquiries + Dashboard). Updated: May 2026

request.description: Requires superadmin authentication and CSRF protection. Creates all parent features and sub-features from FEATURES.DETAILS in the host-creation transaction. Each row uses its own DEFAULT_ENABLED as isEnabled (including 0), REMARKS, and parentFeatureKey (NULL for parent features). Request features cannot override these defaults. TASK_MANAGEMENT is currently disabled by default.

Actor and host come only from authentication. Requires SCHEDULE_VISIT for the resolved assignee; self needs no rule, and Host Admin retains the team override. Other assignees must be active, non-deleted same-host field-app users. Existing customer access is still required. If a restricted customer gains a new assignee, independently requires CUSTOMER_ASSIGNMENT. Open customers and existing assignments remain unchanged. Permission denial returns 403 TEAM_ASSIGNMENT_FORBIDDEN and rolls back all writes. Successful keyed replay preserves original owner/payload checks and customer access without rechecking team permissions. Success retains HTTP 201 and the existing success/message/data envelope.

response.name: Team permission denied

request.description: Requires RESCHEDULE_VISIT for the selected assignee, including the existing other-user assignee when assignedUserId is omitted. Self needs no rule; Host Admin retains the team override. Existing host and customer access checks still apply; self eligibility does not grant access. Changing the assignee adds them only to restricted customers and independently requires CUSTOMER_ASSIGNMENT if they are not already assigned. No customer permission check occurs if no assignment is added. Permission denial returns 403 TEAM_ASSIGNMENT_FORBIDDEN before writes. Existing keyed replay, revision increments, history and HTTP 200 success/message/data response remain unchanged.

response.name: Team permission denied

request.description: Existing read-only revision lookup with authenticated host/customer access. Returns success/data with contractVersion, hostId, userId, visitId and revision. Does not grant permission to mutate; execute-v2 validates the selected assignee.

Existing V2 contract: assignedUserId, expectedRevision, idempotencyKey and remarks are required. After access, replay and revision/status checks, requires RESCHEDULE_VISIT for the selected assignee even when unchanged, plus CUSTOMER_ASSIGNMENT only if a restricted customer gains that assignee. Self needs no rule; Host Admin retains the team override. Denial returns 403 TEAM_ASSIGNMENT_FORBIDDEN without a stored operation or mutation. Revision/status rejections and successful replays retain their recorded outcomes and HTTP 200 success/data contract.

response.name: Team permission denied

request.description: Phase 4 eligibility only. action is exactly CUSTOMER_ASSIGNMENT, SCHEDULE_VISIT or RESCHEDULE_VISIT. Actor/host come from JWT context; body hostId/userId/actorId cannot override them. Self is always included in the database candidate set using the actual ID/name, regardless of memberships, rules, search or field-app access. Everyone is sorted by name ASC then ID, with no duplicate or separately pinned actor. Other users require active memberships/teams, a direct enabled permission rule, active/non-deleted status and, for visits, isFieldAppUser = 1. No admin, missing-configuration or transitive fallback for others. Optional search (100 characters). Supplying either page or limit enables normal pagination over the combined set (defaults 1/10, maximum 100); omitting both returns all eligible users without pagination metadata. The actor appears on their sorted page when paginated. Unsupported action returns 400 VALIDATION_ERROR. Does not modify customers, Visit Plans, login or sync.

Returns feature keys stored with isEnabled = 1 for the supplied hostId (a positive integer), only when parentFeatureKey is NULL or the parent also has isEnabled = 1 for the same host. Children of disabled or missing parents are excluded. No eligible rows returns data.enabled = []. Invalid hostId returns HTTP 400.

item.name: Task Management
item.description: Admin management operations use /api/v1/admin/tasks and the existing admin role/CSRF middleware. Employee operations use /api/v1/app/task. Task responses retain { success, message, data }. Creation requires taskCategoryId. Task list/detail/Kanban include taskCategoryId, taskCategory and tags: [{ id, name, color, isEnabled, isDeleted }]. Historical disabled/deleted tag references remain readable. Optional filters.taskCategoryId, filters.tagId or filters.tagIds (OR matching) narrow lists/Kanban without duplicate tasks or changed pagination. [] means no tag filter. Run docs/TASK_TAGS.sql manually before deploying the tag-enabled backend; do not also run its migration. See Task_Management.postman_collection.json for detailed examples.

item.name: Task Tags
item.description: Admin-only master; authenticated host scope, existing support and CSRF policies. Trimmed names max 50, color #RRGGBB, description max 255. Names are case-insensitively unique within a host INCLUDING soft-deleted tags. Physical deletes are never used. Assignment soft-removes only enabled/non-deleted tag mappings; disabled/deleted historical references are preserved, including when tagIds is []. Task fields and lifecycle timestamps never change.

request.description: Returns all non-deleted data.tags sorted by name ASC. Optional search (max 50) and numeric isEnabled (0/1). No pagination.
name/color required; description/isEnabled optional. Returns data.tag. Duplicate non-deleted names for this host return 409, including disabled tags; deleted names can be reused.

exec: const r = pm.response.json(); if (r.success) pm.environment.set('TASK_TAG_ID', r.data.tag.id);

request.description: tagId plus at least one of name/color/description/isEnabled. isEnabled is optional numeric 0/1 and can be changed alongside other fields. Returns data.tag.
Returns data.tag for a non-deleted tag, including disabled tags.
Returns data.tagId. Historical mappings remain readable with isDeleted: 1; deleted names can be reused.
Explicit numeric isEnabled 0/1. Returns data.tag. Disabled tags cannot be newly assigned.

Returns data: { taskId, tags }. Replaces active assignments in a transaction; [] removes all active assignments. Historical disabled/deleted references remain, and may be retained in tagIds only if already linked. Removed mappings are restored rather than duplicated on reassignment. No task fields or timestamps change.
Returns data.tags: [{ id, name, color }], enabled and non-deleted only, sorted by name ASC. Optional search max 50; no pagination. Employee JWT required; no master mutations are exposed.

Same replacement/history contract as admin, restricted to tasks assigned to the authenticated employee. Empty tagIds removes active assignments; disabled/deleted historical references remain. Returns data: { taskId, tags }.

item.name: Task Categories (Admin)
item.description: Uses ADMIN_TOKEN and matching CSRF cookie/header. All scope comes from authentication. Unix timestamps, active name/prefix uniqueness per host, read-only nextTaskNumber. No category operation renumbers existing tasks.

request.description: Returns data.categories for the authenticated host, including enabled and disabled non-deleted categories and taskCount. Supports the admin list's optional search, isEnabled, sorting and pagination.

All fields optional. Default {} returns ALL matching categories without a pagination key. Supply page or limit to paginate, e.g. { page: 1, limit: 20 }; the omitted parameter defaults to page 1 or limit 20 (limit max 100). Paginated responses include pagination: { page, limit, total, totalPages }. Optional search matches name; isEnabled is 0/1 (omit for both). sortBy: id/name/createdAt/updatedAt; default name ASC. Each category includes taskCount.

Trimmed name (1-100) and prefix (1-20) required. Optional description (max 500/null) and isEnabled (0/1, default 1). Counter starts at 1. Duplicate non-deleted name/prefix returns 409, including disabled categories; PRJ and PRJ- share the same namespace. Returns data.category.

Requires at least one editable field: name, description, prefix, isEnabled. isEnabled is optional numeric 0/1 and can be changed alongside other fields. nextTaskNumber is read-only. Prefix changes only affect future tasks and never reset the sequence. Returns data.category.
Returns data.category including taskCount (all associated tasks). Deleted/missing/cross-host IDs return 404.
Set isEnabled to 0 or 1. Deleted categories cannot be enabled. Disabling only blocks new task selection/reassignment. Returns data.category.
Soft deletion only. Any associated task prevents deletion with 409 TASK_CATEGORY_IN_USE; no tasks are modified. Returns data: { taskCategoryId }.

Returns { status: 'success', timestamp: 'YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm A', data: { columns } }. Same optional filters and sorting as getTasks: assignedToUserId (employee), search (task number OR title), status (database enum), priority, createdByUserId, customerId, visitId, dueDate, completedDate, dueFrom/dueTo and overdueOnly. Nested filters take precedence over top-level filters. Use { hostId: 7 } for all tasks in host 7. All matching tasks are returned without pagination, with four fixed columns TODO/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/OVERDUE and taskCount equal to tasks.length. Deleted/CANCELLED tasks are excluded. Overdue pending/in-progress tasks (dueAt < current Unix second) appear only in OVERDUE, not TODO/IN_PROGRESS. Cards preserve database status and the full getTasks fields/user associations. Card dates use host formats; top-level timestamp uses the host timezone and fixed format above. Empty columns remain present with tasks: []. See Task_Management.postman_collection.json for detailed rules and response assertions. assignedToUserId accepts a single positive ID or an array of positive IDs (for example [47, 48]); array values match ANY selected employee, while all other filters combine with AND. An empty array [] means no employee filter. Duplicate IDs are deduplicated; invalid IDs or array entries return HTTP 400. Required top-level hostId must be a positive safe integer (or digit-only numeric string). Payload/authenticated host matching is temporarily disabled; a different valid payload hostId is accepted but does not change the query scope. Missing/invalid hostId returns HTTP 400 INVALID_HOST_ID. Queries always use the authenticated host, never an untrusted payload scope.

All-time statistics for the authenticated admin's host; a top-level hostId is required and no filters are supported. Returns { success, message, data: { timestamp, summary, statusDistribution, priorityDistribution, userTasksMetrics } } with host-local timestamp. statusDistribution contains TODO, IN_PROGRESS, OVERDUE in that order; COMPLETED is excluded. OVERDUE uses color #c00404. summary.pendingTasks is the non-overdue PENDING count and summary.overduePercentage is overdue / totalTasks * 100, rounded to 2 decimals (0 when totalTasks is 0). Excludes deleted/CANCELLED tasks. PENDING maps to TODO. Overdue pending/in-progress tasks (dueAt < current Unix second) count only in OVERDUE, never TODO/IN_PROGRESS. Summary percentages use distribution count / totalTasks * 100 (2 decimals). userTasksMetrics entries contain only userId, name, profileImageUrl, pendingCount, inProgressCount and overdueCount; assignedCount, completedCount and efficiencyRate are not returned. Only users with pendingCount > 0 or inProgressCount > 0 are returned in userTasksMetrics; completed-only users are omitted without affecting dashboard totals. Overdue tasks with PENDING/IN_PROGRESS status remain eligible. Users are ordered by assignedCount descending then userId ascending; inactive users remain included, deleted/missing profiles return null name/profileImageUrl without dropping their tasks. Empty hosts return zeros and an empty userTasksMetrics array. See Task_Management.postman_collection.json for response assertions. priorityDistribution always contains HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, URGENT in that order, each with { priority, label, count, color }. Colors: HIGH #f97316, MEDIUM #3b82f6, LOW #94a3b8, URGENT #ef4444. Priority counts exclude COMPLETED tasks; overdue tasks remain included, and cancelled/deleted tasks are excluded. Empty priorities return count 0. Required top-level hostId must be a positive safe integer (or digit-only numeric string). Payload/authenticated host matching is temporarily disabled; a different valid payload hostId is accepted but does not change the query scope. Missing/invalid hostId returns HTTP 400 INVALID_HOST_ID. Queries always use the authenticated host, never an untrusted payload scope.

taskCategoryId is required: choose an enabled, non-deleted category in the authenticated host. Missing/invalid IDs return 400, missing/deleted/cross-host categories 404, disabled categories 400. Category prefix/counter allocation, PENDING task, CREATED log and optional attachment commit atomically under a category row lock. Existing task numbers are preserved. Historical number collisions return 409 TASK_NUMBER_CONFLICT and roll back without consuming a number. hostId and creator come only from the token. See Task_Management.postman_collection.json for detailed category examples.

Use an admin JWT and matching admin CSRF cookie/header. Send taskCategoryId (required, enabled/non-deleted category owned by the authenticated host), title and assignedToUserId as multipart text fields. Uses the same locked category allocator as createTask. Other task fields and file are optional. File supports JPEG/PNG/WEBP/PDF up to 10 MB; let Postman set Content-Type. Returns data.task and optional data.attachment. Task, activity, category counter and attachment metadata commit together; failures roll back and clean uploaded media. Notifications run after commit. Do not send taskId/taskCommentId.

Returns { success, message, data: { tasks, pagination } }. Non-admin users see only their assigned tasks. Optional filters.dueDate and filters.completedDate accept YYYY-MM-DD or DD/MM/YYYY strings, for example 2026-10-23 or 23/10/2026. Formats can be mixed in one request. The client's configured host timezone (HostSettings timezone, also used for response formatting) determines inclusive start/end-of-day Unix seconds for dueAt/completedAt comparisons, including DST. Both filters combine with AND; omit unused dates. Invalid dates, timestamps or null return HTTP 400. Legacy dueFrom/dueTo Unix bounds remain supported but cannot be combined with dueDate.

Creates a PENDING task for an eligible field-app user in the authenticated host. Requires title, enabled taskCategoryId and assignedToUserId. Returns data.task. Creating for someone else does not grant ongoing access.
Multipart creation for an eligible user in the authenticated host. Optional JPEG, PNG, WEBP or PDF file up to 10 MB. Let Postman set Content-Type. Returns data.task and optional data.attachment.
Updates editable fields only for a task currently assigned to the employee. Unassigned or cross-host tasks return 404.
Reassigns a currently assigned task to an eligible user in the authenticated host. The previous assignee loses access after reassignment. Unassigned or cross-host tasks return 404.

Admin-only tenant task list. Include the CSRF cookie and matching ADMIN_CSRF_TOKEN header. Optional filters.dueDate and filters.completedDate accept YYYY-MM-DD or DD/MM/YYYY strings interpreted in the client's configured host timezone (HostSettings timezone), matching response formatting. Formats can be mixed in one request. Each becomes inclusive local-day Unix-second bounds on dueAt/completedAt, including DST. Both filters combine with AND; omit unused dates. Invalid dates, timestamps and null return HTTP 400. Legacy dueFrom/dueTo Unix bounds remain supported but cannot be combined with dueDate. Success retains { success, message, data: { tasks, pagination } }. assignedToUserId accepts a single positive ID or an array of positive IDs (for example [47, 48]); array values match ANY selected employee, while all other filters combine with AND. An empty array [] means no employee filter. Duplicate IDs are deduplicated; invalid IDs or array entries return HTTP 400.
Returns task details and up to 10 recent comments, attachments, and activity records.

Admin-only tenant task details with up to 10 recent comments, attachments, and activity records. Each comment includes an attachments array containing attachments linked to that comment; task-level attachments remain in task.attachments. Include the CSRF cookie and matching ADMIN_CSRF_TOKEN header.
Updates editable metadata and writes an UPDATED activity record only when values change. Assignment is handled separately.
Validates an active field-app employee and records the old/new assignee in the activity log.
Admin-authorized start operation. Include the CSRF cookie and matching ADMIN_CSRF_TOKEN header.
Admin-authorized completion. Include the CSRF cookie and matching ADMIN_CSRF_TOKEN header.

Admin-only status override; status must be PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, or CANCELLED. Any transition between these values is allowed, and a status activity record is written. remarks is optional. Include the CSRF cookie and matching ADMIN_CSRF_TOKEN header.
Admin-authorized cancellation. Include the CSRF cookie and matching ADMIN_CSRF_TOKEN header.
Returns immutable chronological task activity with pagination.
Adds a task comment as the authenticated admin.

Creates a task comment and optionally its linked attachment atomically as the authenticated admin. Required: taskId and comment (1-5000 characters). Omit the file part to add a comment without an attachment, or include one JPEG, PNG, WEBP, or PDF file up to 10 MB. Optional remarks: up to 500 characters. Include the CSRF cookie and matching ADMIN_CSRF_TOKEN header. Postman sets the multipart boundary. Success always returns data.comment and includes data.attachment only when a file is uploaded; attachment.taskCommentId is set to the new comment ID. Uploaded media is deleted if persistence fails.
Returns chronological task comments with pagination.
Multipart upload as admin. Include the CSRF cookie and matching ADMIN_CSRF_TOKEN header.
Returns task attachment metadata with pagination.
Returns task attachment metadata after checking admin access to its parent task.
Assigned employee or admin starts a PENDING task. Repeated starts are idempotent.
Completes an IN_PROGRESS task, stores completedAt, and writes remarks to the activity log.
Cancels a PENDING or IN_PROGRESS task and stores cancellation remarks in the activity log.
Returns immutable task activity in chronological order with pagination.
Adds a non-empty comment (maximum 5000 characters); author and tenant come from authentication.
Returns chronological task comments with pagination.
Multipart upload field `file`; supports JPEG, PNG, WEBP, and PDF up to 10 MB. Optional taskCommentId and remarks fields.
Returns task attachment metadata with pagination.
Returns metadata only when the authenticated user can access the parent task.

request.description: Stores the latest snapshot for a device registered to the authenticated user. All timestamps are Unix seconds. Replace example IDs and timestamps. Created, updated and exact duplicate return 200; older and same-second conflicting snapshots return 409 and are not acknowledged. Android blocks the rejected pending snapshot. Client clocks and installation resets prevent strict ordering; see docs/device-health-sync.md.

request.description: Returns all non-deleted field-app users for the authenticated employee's host, matching the admin getUsers scope. Each user contains only userId and name, ordered by name ASC (userId ASC for ties). No pagination or filters. No request fields are required; any supplied hostId, page, limit or filters cannot change the scope or results. Inactive users are included, as in the unfiltered admin API. Empty results return data.users: [].
Returns enabled, non-deleted customers with no active user assignment or an active assignment to the authenticated user. Response: { success, message, data: customers[] }.

item.name: Admin
item.description: Admin portal endpoints - requires admin authentication

item.name: Team Assignment Rules
item.description: Phase 3: rule storage/admin management only, not eligibility or enforcement. Same-team and many-to-many directional rules are supported. Host comes from authenticated admin context.

request.description: Validates both teams in the authenticated host. Same-team rules are valid. Permission flags are independent numeric 0/1 and default to 0; isEnabled defaults to 1 and cannot be supplied on create. Duplicates, including disabled rules, return 409 TEAM_ASSIGNMENT_RULE_EXISTS. A deleted pair restores its existing ID with fresh permission values. Returns { success, message, data: { rule } }.

Both filters are optional. Lists non-deleted rules only; disabled rules are included unless isEnabled is filtered. Includes sourceTeamName/targetTeamName and sourceTeam/targetTeam summaries (id, teamName, isEnabled, isDeleted). This does not calculate assignment eligibility. Returns { success, message, data: { rules } }. Allowed in read-only support sessions.

Changes only supplied permission flags/isEnabled (numeric 0/1); at least one is required. Supplied sourceTeamId/targetTeamId are rejected with 400; host cannot change. Unknown/deleted/foreign-host rules return 404 TEAM_ASSIGNMENT_RULE_NOT_FOUND. Returns { success, message, data: { rule } }.
Soft-deletes and disables the rule, retaining the unique pair for reactivation via create. Returns { success, message, data: { ruleId } }. Blocked in read-only support sessions.

item.name: Teams
item.description: Phase 2: host-scoped functional teams and memberships only. Membership grants no assignment permission. All host IDs come from the authenticated admin or switched-session context. Read-only support permits only list/detail/member-list.

request.description: Trims a required 1-100 character name. isEnabled defaults to 1. Non-deleted names are case-insensitively unique per host; duplicates return 409 TEAM_NAME_EXISTS. Returns { success, message, data: { team } }.

Lists non-deleted teams for the authenticated host. Optional search/page/limit; defaults 1/10, maximum limit 100. Returns { success, message, data: { teams, pagination: { total, page, limit, totalPages } } }.
Returns { success, message, data: { team, members } }. Includes enabled and disabled memberships with minimal user summaries. Unknown/deleted/foreign-host teams return 404 TEAM_NOT_FOUND.
Updates only teamName/isEnabled; at least one is required. Host cannot change. Flags must be numeric 0/1. Returns { success, message, data: { team } }.
Soft-deletes the team with deletedAt. Membership rows remain unchanged; the name can be reused. Returns { success, message, data: { teamId } }.
Returns { success, message, data: { members } }, including disabled rows and a host-scoped user summary. Requires a non-deleted team in the authenticated host.

userId accepts a single positive ID or a non-empty array, e.g. {"teamId":1,"userId":[2,3]}. Adds non-deleted same-host users or reactivates disabled memberships preserving ID/createdAt. Repeated IDs are processed once, in user ID ascending order. An active duplicate returns 409 TEAM_MEMBER_EXISTS with the affected user's database name only, e.g. Alice is already a member of this team. Any invalid/foreign user or write failure rolls back the entire batch; unknown/foreign users receive a generic message. User IDs are not printed in member error messages. Multiple teams per user are allowed. Scalar input returns data: { member }; array input returns data: { members }, including one-element arrays.

userId accepts a single positive ID or a non-empty array, e.g. {"teamId":1,"userId":[2,3],"isEnabled":0}. Applies the same numeric isEnabled (0/1) to all selected memberships. Identity and host cannot be rebound. Repeated IDs are processed once in user ID ascending order; unknown/foreign users or missing memberships return 404 and roll back the entire batch. Missing-member errors include the same-host database name only, e.g. Team membership not found for Alice; unknown/foreign users receive a generic message. User IDs are not printed in member error messages. Scalar input returns data: { member }; array input returns data: { members }.

userId accepts a single positive ID or a non-empty array, e.g. {"teamId":1,"userId":[2,3]}. Disables selected memberships without physical deletion; repeated removal remains disabled. Repeated IDs are processed once in user ID ascending order. Any invalid/foreign user, missing membership or write failure rejects and rolls back the entire batch. Missing-member errors include the same-host database name only, e.g. Team membership not found for Alice; unknown/foreign users receive a generic message. User IDs are not printed in member error messages. Scalar input returns data: { member }; array input returns data: { members }.

Read the latest health snapshot. Optionally provide deviceId; otherwise the active registration with the highest ID is selected. Timestamps are formatted using the host timezone and date-time format. Returns data.deviceHealth = null when no snapshot or active device exists. hostId must match the authenticated host.
